artifact_inventory.description: Deterministic NumPy checks of the endpoint-mode closed form, rotated endpoint-spectrum objective monotonicity, the interior annihilation/revival identity, and the three-dimensional asymptotic spike family.
Verified output of the deterministic numerical checks.

limitations: Exact arithmetic, unconstrained real SPD quadratics, exact spectral endpoints, classical constant strongly-convex Nesterov momentum, and standard zero-momentum initialization only. Loose endpoint bounds, alternate initialization, other accelerated schemes, composite or nonquadratic objectives, restart variants, inexact gradients, and finite precision are outside the theorem. The unbounded quantity is a local relative objective ratio and does not imply divergence or unbounded absolute objective values. Older semi-iterative and polynomial-acceleration literature leaves residual historical-equivalence risk.
record_title: Three-dimensional onset of objective spikes in exact-parameter Nesterov acceleration
scientific_context: For the classical strongly-convex Nesterov method on real SPD quadratics with exact spectral endpoints and standard initialization, endpoint-only spectra are objective-monotone. Every two-dimensional instance therefore has monotone objective values, while a three-dimensional instance exists for every kappa>1 whose local ratio f(x_3)/f(x_2) is unbounded over nonstationary initial points. The mechanism is an interior curvature mode annihilated at step two and revived by momentum at step three.
